q: 1. The direct stress induced in a long column is ............. as compared to bending stress.
explain: For long, slender columns where buckling (bending) effects dominate, the direct (axial) stress component is comparatively negligible relative to the bending stress induced by buckling.

q: 2. A column that fails due to direct stress, is called
explain: A column that fails primarily by crushing (direct compressive stress reaching material strength, without significant buckling) is classified as a short column.

q: 3. A vertical column has two moments of inertia (i.e., Ixx and Iyy). The column will tend to buckle in the direction of the
options: perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: A column buckles about the axis with the minimum moment of inertia (and correspondingly minimum radius of gyration), since that direction offers the least resistance to bending/buckling.

q: 4. The slenderness ratio is the ratio of
options: area of column to least radius of gyration
length of column to least radius of gyration
least radius of gyration to area of column
least radius of gyration to length of column
explain: By definition, slenderness ratio = effective length of column / least radius of gyration.

q: 5. The column whose slenderness ratio is less than 80, are known as
explain: Columns with a relatively low slenderness ratio (below about 80) are classified as short columns, where crushing rather than buckling governs failure.

q: 6. A column with maximum equivalent length has
options: one end fixed and the other end hinged
one end fixed and the other end free
explain: A column with one end fixed and the other completely free has the largest effective length (Le = 2L), the maximum among the standard end conditions.

q: 7. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops on
explain: Horizontal (longitudinal) shear stress exists on every horizontal plane within a beam's depth (complementary to the vertical transverse shear), varying parabolically with depth.

q: 8. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive stress develops on
explain: For a simply supported rectangular beam under a typical downward transverse load, the beam sags, causing the top fibre to experience maximum compressive stress.
